title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and moved quickly through their light agenda.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order and opened the floor to public comment, calling on Stacey Earleywine who was asking for an accommodation for the Nostalgia Theater for an event this weekend.  Earleywine said they are hosting their 2nd Haunted Theater and are excited to now be able to use the basement and described how patrons will work their way through the building and will exit through the rear, which empties directly onto Railroad St.  She is asking to set up a barricade so people can safely exit in that area from 7:00-11:00pm on Friday, October 23rd and Saturday, October 24th.  A motion was made and seconded and the measure was adopted unanimously.

Next, the council approved the meeting agenda and the consent agenda.  The latter included the past meeting minutes, the September Police Activity Report, Building and Zoning Report and Treasurer’s Report and the Warrant List for the for first half of October.

In regular business, Mayor Spicer announced that there is a special meeting scheduled for October 27th at 4:30pm for the presentation of the City of Flora’s Annual Audit.  The mayor then polled commissioners for their comments.  Commissioners Jeremy Henderson used his time to ask if there was an update on the grants for the downtown area.  Flora City Administrator Mike Stanford stated that there was not any new information to share on that topic.  Commissioner Phil Wiley encouraged everyone to check out Nostalgia’s Haunted Theater this Friday and Saturday from 7:00-11:00pm.  He continued by noting that with the nice weather, people will be out walking around the community.  He encouraged them to dress to be seen for safety’s sake and not dress in black for the Halloween season as its definitely harder to see people in dark clothing while you’re driving and not expecting people to be on the road.  So again, dress to be seen.

Commissioner Lacey Lewis reminds everyone about the upcoming Flora Halloween Parade and also made a pitch for everyone to pay a final visit to the Community Harvest Market this Saturday from 8:00am-2:00pm at Library Park on North Main Street in front of the Flora Public Library.  A full slate of events are scheduled for the whole family including; their usual farm to table farmer’s market, food trucks and other product vendors, a gift basket raffle, a soup cookoff, children’s inflatables and yard games, pumpkin painting, a puppy costume parade and an apple cider/hot cocoa/harvest treat cup fundraiser.  There’s also live music throughout the day plus, a cornhole tournament organized by Joey Persinger.  There’s also a featured activity that offers you an invitation to test your skills at the Shooting Simulator Trailer.  Challenge your friends and see how you measure up in this fun, hi-tech, interactive experience!  Whether you’re competitive or just looking to try something new, you won’t want to miss the Shooting Simulator Tailer.

City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford presented an ordinance for the consideration of commissioners.  The measure authorizes the execution of an agreement with the Illinois Municipal League Risk Management Association Premium Agreement.  It calls for the City of Flora to receive a one percent discount for paying the annual premium of $297,313 by November 13, 2026.  Stanford stated that is same amount paid last year, so there is not an increase for the new policy.  Commissioner Jeremy Henderson asked how that could happen.  Stanford chalked it up to the flip-flopping of property claims and workers compensation from the previous year.  Commissioners approved the ordinance without dissent.  Stanford also took a moment to address the roof leak at the Flora Public Library.  The vendor was in the middle of roof repairs when last week’s rains came and caused damage to a multitude of ceiling tiles.  He said the company is bonded and insurance claims will likely follow.  Thanks to the effort of city workers, the Flora Public Library will re-open Tuesday (today) for its regular operating hours.

Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles presented an ordinance to grant a variance to Gene and Jana Darrough at 1115 Clan Street to open a nail salon.  The measure was passed unanimously.  Bayles also offered his thanks to public service workers and Toby Rinehart for their work cleaning up the library.

And Superintendent of Public Services Toby Rinehart commented on the roadwork that was planned at Charley Brown Park last week.  As the work crew milled the road and prepared to oil and chip the road, heavy rains came and set the effort back.  Rinehart explained that they will give it another try this Wednesday and Thursday with better weather and results expected.  So, look for the roads at Charley Brown Park to be closed those days.

title: FLORA SCHOOL BOARD
full_story:
The Flora School Board met last night, greenlighting several district updates and celebrating a big achievement for local athletes.

In business news, the board approved its consent agenda, which includes a maintenance grant submission for roof work at Flora High School, a seventh-grade field trip to a hockey game in Evansville next month, and the annual tradition of providing Christmas hams and turkeys for district staff.

The board also took time to recognize the Floyd Henson Junior High baseball team for their standout season and making it all the way to the state tournament.

In personnel changes, the district employed Jacob Oldendorf as a full-time custodian, accepted the resignation of custodian Kevin Macarthy, and approved the retirement of Beverly Wood, effective late next month.

Superintendent Dr. Hackney also praised families for their turnout at recent parent-teacher conferences and looked ahead to the upcoming Veterans Day Program.

title: AG HANDLES POACHING CASE
full_story:
The Illinois Attorney General’s Office will handle the deer poaching case of Wayne County Board member Steven K. Manning, 45, of Wayne City.

Illinois Conservation Police made the arrest Saturday night, October 10th and issued a dozen citations, including hunting with a firearm during archery season, using a silencer on his firearm and spotlighting deer.

Due to a number of conflicts, the Wayne County State’s Attorney cannot prosecute the Manning case.  State’s Attorney Kyle Ellis serves as the attorney for the county and Manning is a county board member, serving on the finance committee.

Additionally, the case cannot be assigned to the Illinois Appellate Prosecutor’s Office because Wayne County has a contract with that office to handle various cases.  As a result, it will ultimately be up to lawyers with the Illinois Attorney General’s Office which charges will be prosecuted and if any of those charges rise to the level of a felony offense.

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Flora Chief of Police Jeremy Ruger released his Activity Report for September during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

During the month, Flora police officers investigated 11 traffic accidents.

They made seven criminal arrests.  There were four drug arrests and one DUI arrest during September.  There were four local ordinance arrests, 13 traffic arrests and six warrant arrests.

Officers issued 22 warning tickets, responded to 18 alarms and had 1,063 calls for service and had no juvenile contacts.

Also, Flora police officers drove 5,055 miles and conducted 74 investigations during September.  They answered 299, 911 calls and conducted 11 UTV Inspections and 1 Golf Cart Inspection during September.

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
One quarter of the state’s winter wheat crop was planted last week, according to USDA, pushing planting pace to 53% just ahead of the five-year average as of October 18th.

In the latest USDA crop and progress report released on Monday there were 5 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending October 18th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 63.3 degrees, 8 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 0.79 inches, 0.05 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated 8% very short, 24% short, 63% adequate, and 5% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 13% very short, 25% short, 58% adequate, and 4% surplus.

Corn mature reached 98%, compared to the 5-year average of 97%.  Corn harvested reached 63%, compared to the 5-year average of 58%.  Corn condition was rated 3% very poor, 8% poor, 29% fair, 46% good, and 14% excellent.

Soybeans dropping leaves reached 97%, equal to the 5-year average.  Soybeans harvested reached 66%, compared to the 5-year average of 62%.

Winter wheat planted reached 53%, compared to the 5-year average of 51%.  Winter wheat emerged reached 22%, compared to the 5-year average of 25%.

title: FLORA BUILDING AND ZONING REPORT
full_story:
Flora Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles presented the monthly building and zoning report for September during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

The report shows six new residential construction projects were undertaken in September, valued at $37,637.

There was one new commercial project started during September, valued at $750,000.

And there was one new industrial miscellaneous project started during September, valued at $138,371.

There was a total of eight new projects in Flora, valued at $926,008 with $495 collected in permit fees and $100 in deposit fees collected for September.

The year-to-date figures show that there are 52 total residential projects so far this year with a value of $705,076.  There are 11 year-to-date commercial projects valued at $18,507,334 and one new industrial project valued at $138,371.

That makes 63 total projects valued at $19,350,781, with $4,238 in permit fees and $1,200 in deposit fees collected for 2026.

title: IFB ANNUAL MEETING
full_story:
Scott McKain, an internationally recognized keynote speaker, business strategist and bestselling author known for his work on customer experience, differentiation and helping organizations stand out in competitive markets, will be the keynote speaker during Illinois Farm Bureau’s Annual Meeting.

This year’s meeting, with the theme “Farming for the Next Generation,” will be December 12th through 15th at the Hyatt Regency in Chicago.  McKain will speak Saturday night, with the president’s address Sunday morning.

McKain has spent more than three decades consulting and speaking for companies around the world, delivering more than 2,000 keynote presentations on leadership, relevance and creating distinction in business.

McKain is the author of several acclaimed business books, including “Create Distinction,” “ICONIC,” “The Ultimate Customer Experience” and “Beyond Distinction.”  His presentations focus on helping organizations build lasting customer relationships, create unique value and remain relevant in rapidly changing markets.

Illinois Farm Bureau also announced more than a dozen micro talks will be available to meeting attendees December 12th and 13th.  A tradition at Annual Meeting, the talks bring experts and members together to share information on popular agricultural topics.

Attendees can also expect the return of charitable auctions, ice cream fundraiser, Young Leader Discussion Meets and awards programs.

“Annual Meeting provides the IAA Foundation an excellent opportunity to raise funds to further our charitable mission.  We are grateful to members and local businesses who donate items to place on the in-person, online and live auctions, and we are currently seeking additional donations for this year’s lineup,” IAA Foundation Director Susan Moore said.

Anyone interested in donating an item for auction can visit iaafoundation.org for more details or visit your county Farm Bureau. Donations are appreciated by November 2nd.

The deadline to register for Annual Meeting is November 13th.  Contact your county Farm Bureau to register.

title: UNEMPLOYMENT RATE DOWN
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Employment Security (IDES) announced that the unemployment rate was 4.6% in September, down 0.1 percentage point from August, and up 0.1 percentage point from the same month, one year ago, based on data provided by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS).  The revised August unemployment rate was 4.7%.

Total nonfarm payrolls decreased over-the-month in September, down 7,200 (0.1%) to 6,164,500.  The August monthly change in payrolls was revised from the preliminary report, from down 4,400 to down 8,300.  The September payroll jobs estimate and unemployment rate reflect activity for the week including the 12th.

The industry sectors with the largest monthly payroll jobs increases included: Leisure and Hospitality up 5,700, Construction up 1,300, and Financial Activities up 400.  The sectors with the largest over-the-month jobs decreases included: Government down 4,600, Private Education and Health Services down 3,700, and Professional and Business Services down 2,400.

Compared to a year ago, total nonfarm payroll jobs were up 13,800 jobs.  The industry groups with the largest jobs increases included: Construction up 14,300, Leisure and Hospitality up 8,500, and Private Education and Health Services up 5,400. The industry groups with the largest jobs decreases included: Financial Activities down 13,500, Information down 3,000 and Trade, Transportation and Utilities down 2,800.  In September, total nonfarm payrolls were up 0.2% over-the-year in Illinois and up 0.3% in the nation.

“Despite continued economic uncertainty driven by federal policies, Illinois’ unemployment rate declined for the third consecutive month, a sign of the resilience of Illinois businesses and workers,” said Deputy Governor Andy Manar.  “There is more work to do, and the state remains focused on providing stability where we can, supporting businesses, and connecting Illinoisans with good-paying jobs.”

“The decline in unemployment coupled with the increase in payroll jobs reinforces the importance of investing in our state’s biggest asset – our workforce,” said DCEO Director Kristin Richards.  “DCEO is committed to building upon this momentum by continuing to implement initiatives and programs that create jobs.”

The number of unemployed persons in September was 297,700, down 3.0% from August, and up 1.8% over the same month one year ago.  The labor force was down 0.1% from August and down 1.3% over-the-year.  The unemployment rate identifies those individuals who are out of work and seeking employment.  An individual who exhausts or is ineligible for benefits is still reflected in the unemployment rate if they actively seek work.

IDES helps connect jobseekers to employers who are hiring in a number of ways, including hosting and co-hosting job fairs and hiring events with statewide workforce partners, and through maintaining Illinois JobLink (IJL), the state’s largest job search engine.  Illinois JobLink is a tool used by jobseekers to look for work, and by employers who can post open and available positions for hire and browse resumes.  Recently, Illinois JobLink showed 60,977 posted resumes with 75,535 jobs available.

title: VOTING UNDERWAY
full_story:
While Election Day is still weeks away, thousands of Illinois residents have already voted.

As of October 13th, Matt Dietrich of the Illinois State Board of Elections said approximately 67,000 early votes had already been cast.  Election officials have also received about 202,000 vote-by-mail ballots.

“About 1.1 million people as of right now have requested vote-by-mail ballots, so we know that there are a lot of them that are still outstanding,” Dietrich said, noting he anticipates about 1.3 million vote-by-mail ballots cast in this election as applications don’t close until October 29th.

A gubernatorial race is on the ballot this year with incumbent Governor JB Pritzker facing Republican challenger Darren Bailey.

In addition to governor, voters will see these state offices on their ballot, attorney general, secretary of state, comptroller and treasurer, in the Illinois Senate; 39 of the 59 seats, and in the Illinois House of Representatives all 118 seats.

At the federal level, Democrat Juliana Stratton, Republican Don Tracy and Independent Whitfield Harrington Jr. compete for the US Senate seat vacated by retiring Senator Dick Durbin.  Voters also will elect representatives in all 17 Illinois congressional districts.

On the Clay County ballot voters will choose between incumbent representative Mike Bost and challenger Julie Fortier.  There is also a race for a member of the Clay County Board in District K between David E. Johnson and Rachel Walker.  There will also be Judicial Retention questions on the ballot.

For a ballot preview, Dietrich encouraged voters to visit their county clerk’s website, where specimen ballots are typically posted before Election Day.

Dietrich noted eligible residents can still register during early voting or on Election Day November 3rd at their polling locations, open from 6 am to 7 pm.

“Registration doesn’t close until the polls close on November 3rd,” he said.

Early voting continues through November 2nd.  Dietrich said many jurisdictions added expanded and weekend voting hours, which can be found on the county clerk’s website.

Illinois requires vote-by-mail ballots to be postmarked by November 3rd and received within 14 days of Election Day to be counted.  To avoid potential postal delays, Dietrich encouraged voters to use a designated drop box location, “usually located right outside the county clerk’s office.”

“If you’re voting by mail and you don’t want to put your ballot in the hands of the postal service, you can go directly to the secure drop box to drop it in, and it will be picked up immediately,” he said.  “Your ballot goes from you directly into the hands of your election authority.”

For more information on voting in the 2026 General Election, visit elections.il.gov.
